summary: China's economy grew 4.5% last quarter on strong exports while shoppers held back, and a report says DeepSeek is helping Huawei design its next AI chips.
body: China's National Bureau of Statistics said on Monday that the economy grew 4.5% in July to September compared with a year earlier, up from 4.3% in the spring quarter and a little above what economists expected [^1][^2][^3]. Growth for the first nine months was 4.6%, which keeps the country within this year's official target of 4.5% to 5% [^1][^3]. Factories and exports did most of the work: industrial output rose 5.5% in September, while retail sales, a measure of what households buy in shops and online, grew only 1.1% [^1][^2]. Investment in things like buildings and infrastructure fell 7.2% over the first nine months, and the property market is still shrinking [^1][^2].

For daily life, the numbers point to caution. The official urban unemployment rate was 5.2% in September [^1][^5], but economists told Reuters that figure looks better than reality because anyone who works even one hour a week counts as employed [^1]. The jobless rate for 16-to-24-year-olds not in school reached 18.9% in August, its highest point this year [^5]. A 26-year-old accountant told Reuters her bonus was nearly cut in half [^1]. My read: China is selling a lot to the world, but families at home are still careful with money.

In tech, The Information reported on Oct 19 that Huawei engineers are working inside DeepSeek's offices so that the AI start-up's needs shape Huawei's future Ascend chips (Ascend is Huawei's line of AI processors, a home-grown alternative to Nvidia's) [^4]. DeepSeek reportedly plans to start training models on the Ascend 950DT by the end of this year [^4]. Neither company has commented, and the report says DeepSeek still wants access to Nvidia chips, which remain far more powerful [^4].
